correctness.rationale: Given known N, weighted multipartite Matrix-Tree identity produces exact P_v(z). Its distinguished root at 1-N has multiplicity r-2, recovering r. For each other root -(N-t-1), dividing multiplicity after removing mandatory z by t-1 recovers the count of all non-observed size-t parts. The remaining other classes are singletons and the observed class is the residual of N; all ranges and edge cases N=2, complete graphs, stars, and repeated sizes follow. 2,892 independent exact Laplacian determinant point checks and 336 exact polynomial inversion replays agree for all multipartite partitions of N=2,...,9. Finite replay is corroboration only; infinite proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The inverse problem asks what global graph structure can be inferred from an exact local random-spanning-tree statistic. One arbitrary rooted vertex-degree law determines an unbounded family of multipartite isomorphism types, including nonregular hosts and singleton classes, via an explicit polynomial root decoder without enumerating spanning trees. The known-order hypothesis is mathematically necessary, illustrated by identical deterministic degree-one laws of star leaves of different orders.
